newsitem.title: USA: US stock index futures end higher, relief on rates.
newsitem.headline: US stock index futures end higher, relief on rates.

text.p: U.S. stock index futures ended higher, as the market grew comfortable with the possibility that the Federal Reserve might raise interest rates by 25 basis points at the end of the month, traders and analysts said.
"It was pretty much anticipated that rates would go up," said Bob Dickey, an analyst at Dain Bosworth Inc. "But people were looking for a larger hike."

"There weren't a lot of fundamental factors, just a general sense of relief," said another analyst, adding that the market had been factoring a rate increase of 50 basis points -- not 25 -- earlier in the week.

Several former Federal Reserve officials said they expected a 25-basis-point hike in the Federal funds rate on September 24. One trader said September Standard & Poor 500s "really gapped up" on former Boston Federal Reserve bank president Richard Syron's forecast for a 25-basis-point rate hike.
However, technical factors also played a part in pushing September towards the 660.00 area, traders said. They said buy-stop orders were touched off at the weekly high of 657.30.
More importantly, September S&Ps remained well above the GLOBEX low of 642.00.
"It spiked bottom in GLOBEX and just never looked back," one floor trader said.
September S&Ps fell to 642.00 on GLOBEX, below the one-month low at 642.70, in a kneejerk reaction to the stronger than expected U.S. August labor reports.

Like bonds, S&Ps had priced in the bearish implications of the reports too quickly, too sharply, and soon found commission house buying on the lows. Although there was light fund and institutional selling at the opening of pit trade, buyers prevailed and sent September S&Ps through the 200-day moving average of 652.80 and the resistance level of 653.00.
One analyst said September S&Ps would trade between the 200-day moving average and the 100-day moving average at 662.45 in the near term, with the 660.00 level serving as a pivot point.

Nikkei futures remained firmer, with December still shy of testing resistance at 20,500.00. Traders continued to roll positions into December, from September, ahead of September's expiration on September 12.
One major U.S. institution rolled 2,000 September positions into December when the spread traded at 5.95 to 6.00 points, traders said.
Total estimated volume for S&Ps, including spread trades, was 90,000 contracts, a trader said after the close.
S&P futures backed off their daily highs after U.S. bond futures pared gains before their close at 1400 CDT/1900 GMT, but short-covering popped September above 658.00 at the close.

At the end of pit trade, September S&Ps were 9.25 points higher at 658.25, NYSE New Composites were up 4.60 at 353.75, KBT Value Lines were up 7.70 at 619.80, Nikkeis were up 80.0 at 20,400, Midcaps were 2.90 higher at 232.55 and Nasdaq 100s rose 12.50 to 665.75.
